service-daemon-process-management.rationale: 單實例鎖可借；fork 常駐化暫緩
service-daemon-process-management.note: The previously member-less row is now real: grok wrote xai-grok-workspace-daemon up as a mechanism, so these clauses are citable verbatim - the advisory flock held for the daemon's whole life (the PID text is diagnostic only; exclusion comes from the lock, and a contended acquire returns Ok(None) so the caller exits quietly instead of running a second instance), acquire_or_take_over escalation against a live predecessor (read the recorded PID, signal gracefully, poll for TAKEOVER_GRACE, force kill, poll for TAKEOVER_KILL_GRACE, declining if a newer spawn won the lock instead), the ordering rule that double-fork and setsid must run before anything starts threads (grok daemonizes before it builds the tokio runtime), the shared helper that opens every daemon-owned file (log, pidfile, preview-proxy log) with O_NOFOLLOW and mode 0600, and fail-soft oom_score_adj adjustment. Disposition unchanged at 遠期: the fail-closed single-instance lock is the borrowable half, but the residency half (fork/setsid/chdir to root/stdio repointing) has no Windows equivalent and shipping IH as an installed resident daemon is a product decision rather than a gap; grok itself only daemonizes under --daemonize, which defaults off.

sidecar-supervision-with-backoff-restart.label: 輔助行程監督與健康退避重啟
sidecar-supervision-with-backoff-restart.rationale: IH 無 sidecar 可監督；產品級
sidecar-supervision-with-backoff-restart.note: grok's supervisor execs exactly one child (the preview proxy), captures its stdout/stderr into a daemon-owned log that is served back through the diagnostics endpoints, spawns it with kill_on_drop inside a restart loop whose 1 s base delay doubles to a 30 s cap and RESETS after a run lasting PREVIEW_PROXY_HEALTHY_RUN_SECS so a crash loop converges on a fixed interval, re-checks getppid() beside PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) to close the fork/exec race (which is why the task must run on long-lived workers), and scrapes the child's loopback /__control/activity (idle withholding) and /__control/metrics (preview_proxy_ prefix every 60 s). Gated by --preview-enabled, default off. 遠期 rather than rewrite because the supervised artifact is grok's preview product and IH has no sidecar plane to supervise; the health-resetting backoff and activity-scraped idle detection are the reusable parts.

loopback-readiness-and-log-diagnostics-s.label: 回環就緒狀態與日誌診斷端點
loopback-readiness-and-log-diagnostics-s.rationale: 值得做；就緒契約與日誌尾端上限
loopback-readiness-and-log-diagnostics-s.note: Three unauthenticated GET routes on a loopback-only listener that never goes through the sandbox port mapping: /ready is 200 only when the hub state is Connected and 503 otherwise, with the body served either way so naive HTTP probes and state parsers agree, and its field set is a FROZEN contract with the sandbox readiness gate (additions only, never rename or remove); /statusz flattens those fields plus os and advisory image_capabilities that is explicitly never an authorization input because the guest can forge the markers; /logs tails the daemon log at a 64 KiB default clamped to a 256 KiB hard cap, returns 404 when there is no log file, and answers a generic 500 on I/O error so the log path is never echoed. State latching is deliberately sticky (set_failed is terminal, a 4100-4199 close code survives set_disconnected, revive_connected only for an allow-listed code). Always started by grok's workspace server, which advertises diag: true; the Unix socket is 0600 and the TCP listener exists only on Windows, so DEFAULT_DIAG_PORT is inert on Unix. IH's web surface has no readiness/status/log endpoint, no frozen probe contract and no bounded log-tail read, so this is rewrite, not 已存在.

shared-http-client-pool-with-poison-esca.label: 共用 HTTP 連線池與毒化池逃逸
shared-http-client-pool-with-poison-esca.rationale: 值得做；末次重試逃離毒化池
shared-http-client-pool-with-poison-esca.note: Four shared clients with deliberately different pool policies: an HTTP/2 keepalive general client (30 s pool idle timeout, a client-mode header), an HTTP/1.1-only upload client with pool_max_idle_per_host(2) and a 10 s idle timeout because a degraded multiplexed connection silently drops multipart bodies, a blocking startup client whose STARTUP_FETCH_TIMEOUT is both the connect and the read ceiling, and a pool-less never-cached client. The mechanism is the policy rather than the constructors: send_with_retry_escaping_pool runs early attempts on the pooled client and swaps the LAST attempt of a multi-attempt run onto the pool-less client so a tight budget escapes a reset or GOAWAY immediately instead of waiting for pool eviction, and transport failures are classified by walking the cause chain with certificate verdicts separated from plain connect failures (an untrusted issuer must not read as an unreachable host). Two compile-time asserts pin the budget relationships between the startup timeouts. grok's own moduleCoverage still calls xai-grok-http infrastructure that contributes no mechanism of its own while its hintCorrections assigns the crate to service; the verbatim domains.service entry is what hard rule 1 requires, and that entry itself argues the pool-escape policy plus the classifier are the mechanism. IH has no shared outbound client pool or transport-failure classifier in this domain, so rewrite.

streaming-stt-dictation-with-out-of-proc.label: 串流語音聽寫與行程外麥克風擷取
streaming-stt-dictation-with-out-of-proc.rationale: 依賴外部 STT 服務；產品級緩辦
streaming-stt-dictation-with-out-of-proc.note: A streaming STT client plus a pipeline task rather than a renderer concern: press/release/shutdown commands, binary PCM followed by an audio.done frame on the STT websocket, server events mapped to Created/Partial/Done/Error, a NO_SPEECH_TIMEOUT watchdog that tears down a silent session with microphone guidance instead of streaming a dead input, and a bounded BACKLOG_MAX_CHUNKS backlog so capture never backpressures during the handshake (holding the sender defers the writer's audio.done until the backlog drains). Capture is deliberately out of process, where the audio stack is expensive: the binary re-execs itself as a hidden __mic-capture helper speaking a one-line READY handshake, Linux falls back to system recorders probed with a short --raw check, and the whole feature is compile-time gated by the audio cargo feature. grok's hintCorrections moved xai-grok-voice into service (hintWas interface) because it is an outbound service integration plus an event stream, which is why it is this domain's business. 遠期: real and well bounded, but a hosted STT dependency plus microphone capture is a product-level addition with no IH counterpart.

inert-permission-context-logging.label: 權限情境上報記錄（未接線）
inert-permission-context-logging.rationale: 對廠商遙測且全程未接線，不做

unmergedDoubts.whyNotMerged: Both are 'one process/binary serving several service roles' and codex's modules list includes exec-server. Re-examined on this re-run now that grok's daemon mechanism has a verbatim name (it was moduleCoverage-only before): still not merged. The codex mechanism's four helper roles (apply-patch, linux sandbox, windows sandbox, filesystem helper) are confinement helpers owned by the safety domain, so the shared content is only the argv[0] multiplexing trick, whereas grok's mechanism is residency plus single-instance exclusion with no role multiplexing at all. The grok half now sits in its own row with a real member instead of a member-less one.

I merged dsh's HTTP carrier into the HTTP service host row because in dsh the webserver route registry IS the registration seam for the /api bridge. One consequence is recorded here: IH's single web-service mechanism describes BOTH its unary HTTP route surface and its one WebSocket mux, and rule 2 lets it appear once, so I placed it in the HTTP row and added an ihNote to the WebSocket mux row and the trust-fence row instead of citing it three times. IH's mux does carry live session streams (chunk/reasoning/agent-state), which is why the WebSocket mux and SSE rows are close cousins of the HTTP row rather than cleanly disjoint.

Upstream splits the listener from the OpenAPI/SDK generator, while the fork bundles listener lifecycle, route-tree composition and lazy /doc into one mechanism and then adds a separate legacy-spec-compat mechanism. I therefore placed the fork's bundle in the listener row and the fork's legacy compat transform in the vendor/codegen row, so the fork's OpenAPI code sits in one row while its listener sits in the other. A reader must not read the fork's bundle as double-counted.

The descriptor generator and the Remote plane are two halves of one design and could be one row; I kept them separate because generation is build tooling with no Cordis plugin row while the plane is the runtime dispatch surface, and merging would also have pulled in the boot/profile seam that composes them, which is a third distinct capability.

All three push or receive server-side state outside the request/response cycle. Not merged because dsh's bridge is an in-tree browser consumer of a Host-event allowlist, codex's relay is an outbound dial to a vendor backend with enrollment, chunking and cursor resume, and dsh's webhook ingress is HMAC-verified inbound ingress from third-party systems: three different trust directions, not one capability.

Both propagate credentials into a live service session. Kept apart because dsh's is a redacted, revisioned, read-through RPC namespace (fail-closed, secrets never serialized) whereas cc-custom's is an unauthenticated stdin frame that mutates process.env directly (fail-open by design). The security posture is opposite, so a merge would hide the difference that matters.

codex's app-server mechanism de facto covers stdio bidirectional JSON-RPC control, so it arguably belongs in the bidirectional SDK stdio row. I kept it out because its distinguishing content is carrier multiplicity (stdio + private 0600 UDS + raw WS + Off, flock-serialised startup, stale-socket unlink) over one shared framed surface, which no other source has; the handshake and backpressure clauses are separate codex mechanisms so they cannot be folded into the same citation either.

The vendor/codegen row is built from codex's generated-contract export plus opencode's OpenAPI/SDK codegen and the fork's legacy spec transform. codex's headless JSONL exec surface names stdout JSONL among its flags, so it could have been routed to the one-way output row instead; I placed it with the export row because its differentiating capability is the --output-schema / --output-last-message machine contract rather than the line format, which is the same 'the published wire contract is a product' idea. cc-custom's output-format/exit-code mechanism stayed in its own row because it is a one-way consumer contract with no generated artifact.

IH's frozen v0 contract carries a session/history replay surface and cc-custom's replay/dedup is an acknowledged input stream over the same stdio channel, so a merge is arguable. Kept separate because IH's is read-side history the client drives explicitly (the server never replays to a fresh subscription) while cc-custom's is write-side idempotence (one uuid executed at most once, duplicates answered with isReplay:true).

Merged into one vendor/codegen row, but the lost detail is real: codex vendors TypeScript plus JSON Schema in two disjoint stable/experimental export sets with zstd-precomputed bundles, while opencode serves a lazily built OpenAPI document and compiles SDK clients behind a manifest. The merged label hides that codex's artifact is schema-for-SDK-authors while opencode's is a served HTTP document.

Merged into one workspace-routing/control-plane row, but the two are not the same maturity: upstream has a RequestPlan parser plus the /experimental/control-plane/move-session operation, while the fork has the full reverse proxy (HTTP and WebSocket) and the x-opencode-sync fence wait. A reader should not read the merged row as 'both do proxying'.

All six are one ACP surface over stdio and are merged, which flattens three differences. (1) Maturity: upstream's adapter is initialize+prompt with runUntilIdle gating, the fork implements the full load/fork/list/resume/close lifecycle. (2) Permission philosophy: IH uses a binary autoApprove switch with no session/request_permission flow (a refused prompt never reaches the session service), dsh downgrades to one-shot allow-once/reject-once so a client response can never become a durable grant, and the opencode pair route prompts through the engine. That divergence is why the row is 已存在 rather than rewrite. (3) NEW on this re-run: grok's two members are the transport half only (channel pair with typed failures, spawn-per-message gateway dispatch, fire-and-forget notifications; bounded stdin reader, one-escape normalizer, line ceiling) and grok's inventory records no lifecycle or permission surface at all, so the merged row mixes four lifecycle implementations with one wire library. The previous pass named xai-acp-lib as the strongest candidate for this row and refused it only because hard rule 1 blocked a moduleCoverage name; with verbatim names the merge is now made, and this entry is the record of what it hides.

Service authentication is split into a launch-token/HMAC-cookie row (dsh) and a Basic-auth-plus-exemptions row (opencode pair, plus codex's capability-token / signed-bearer JWT upgrade gate). One row was arguable; kept apart because they differ in what they bind (an authority-bound signed cookie vs a long-lived static credential) and because codex's is an upgrade-time gate rather than a per-route middleware.

codex and cc-custom both expose the harness itself as an MCP server over stdio and are merged; cc-custom's control-channel bridge stayed separate because it carries MCP traffic in the opposite direction (servers the SDK consumer registered in-process, inside the SDK protocol). Merging would have conflated 'IH as MCP server' with 'MCP over the IH control channel'.

Both belong to xai-grok-workspace-daemon, and the previous pass carried that module as ONE member-less row described as double-fork + pidfile lock + preview-proxy supervision, so a single daemon-process-management row was arguable. Kept as two because the capabilities and their failure postures are opposite: residency and exclusivity fail CLOSED (a contended flock declines and the process exits quietly), while sidecar supervision is fail-SOFT (a spawn or log-open failure backs off and retries, an unreachable proxy is a quiet no-op on the activity path). A merged row would also have hidden that the reusable part - health-resetting restart backoff, PDEATHSIG ordering, activity scraped for idle detection - is not the same capability as daemonizing.

grok's diagnostics server is a SECOND HTTP listener in the same process and was a candidate for the HTTP service host row. Not merged because it is deliberately separate from the main surface: three fixed unauthenticated GET routes on its own loopback or unix-socket bind that never goes through the sandbox port mapping, a /ready field set frozen against an external readiness gate, and /logs serving the daemon's own log - whereas the host-surface row is the main API/UI surface with routing, static serving and authentication, and a merged row would have to explain why an unauthenticated listener is not a trust problem. The same reasoning keeps codex's unauthenticated /healthz and /readyz clauses out of the diagnostics row: they live inside codex:websocket-listener-authentication, and rule 2 forbids citing that mechanism a second time.

Both keep a newline-delimited stdio channel honest and one cross-source row was considered. Kept apart because they defend opposite directions with different policies: cc-custom guards the OUTBOUND stream for line-oriented consumers (escape U+2028 and U+2029, wrap process.stdout.write and divert non-JSON lines to stderr, fail-soft), while grok hardens the INBOUND reader (a depth-64 blocking_send channel so stdin backpressures instead of buffering, a normalizer limited to the one escaped-slash form the pinned acp envelope would drop with everything else forwarded byte-identical, and a 64 MiB line ceiling as a typed error). The only shared property is that the framing layer is a trust boundary; merging would have claimed a shared capability neither source states.

grok's mechanism was merged into the typed-remote-RPC row with dsh, which flattens the halves: dsh's member is the server/dispatch side (decorators, descriptor registry, gateway interception of the shared /api channel, conservative SRC fallback, one RemoteError discriminated by code and never by instanceof) while grok's is the client/contract side (a connected latch with NotConnected fast-fail, a non-retryable WorkspaceHibernated that must NOT clear the latch, adjacently-tagged wire enums, const ACTIVITY with no default so every new RPC method must declare its idle-hibernation class, a turn_active / hub_error / unknown_method envelope with a legacy prefix matcher, plus xai-grok-tools-api's protobuf types and shared save-time/bind-time validation). grok's frozen-contract half was also a candidate for the vendor/codegen row; it was not placed there because that row is about ARTIFACTS exported for consumers (TypeScript plus JSON Schema bundles, a served OpenAPI document, an SDK generator) and grok's contract crate publishes nothing outward.

Placed as its own row, but the crate boundary is genuinely split and a reader should know it: grok's moduleCoverage still files xai-grok-http as infrastructure for the service and ops domains that contributes no mechanism of its own, while the inventory's mechanism entry argues the pool-escape policy and the transport-failure classifier ARE the mechanism, and xai-grok-sampler (model domain) is the consumer that carries the pooled HTTP/2 client plus the pool-less HTTP/1.1 fallback into sampling. A reader who expects voice input under interface should read this entry first: the pipeline, the STT websocket, the no-speech watchdog and the out-of-process mic helper carry no rendering or screen-mode policy, which is what this audit's interface domain covers.
